original_test_intent: Install the approved Linux GUI build from a physical USB key, reboot to a functional graphical environment and verify events contain no unexplained issues.
original_method: A qualified operator verifies/inserts the signed USB, completes the destructive console installer and controlled GUI package/driver setup, then demonstrates local/KVM graphical operation after reboot.
manual_activity: User approves signed media, exact wipe target and graphics/package baseline; qualified operator performs USB install, desktop configuration, display validation and reboot.
required_inputs: Signed/checksummed Linux GUI USB image and supported release
Stable target disk/partition/wipe/boot policy with non-target exclusions
Pinned repository snapshot, package manifest and update policy
GPU/display adapter, monitor/KVM, kernel and signed driver compatibility matrix
Qualified operator, console/OOB, backup/recovery and known-event allowlist
safety_requirements: Verify stable disk target and signed media before format
Do not run broad update/upgrade without pinned approved repository and rollback
Preserve console fallback before installing graphical/driver changes
Stop on target ambiguity, package/driver/display/boot/event/power/BMC fault or recovery loss
Do not enter secrets or automate destructive installer decisions
agent_execution_scope: Record media, storage, package and graphics baseline
Organize operator installer and GUI screenshots
Collect post-boot package/kernel/driver/display/session and event evidence if approved
Do not insert media, partition, upgrade blindly, drive GUI installer or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve image, target, package/driver/display matrix and recovery
Provide qualified operator and own destructive/GUI recovery
Review display, reboot and event evidence to decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly identifies the task as manual; source apt commands express package intent but are unsafe without a pinned release/repository and compatibility plan.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use operator-controlled USB install and approved pinned package manifest; gather read-only post-boot display-server, desktop-session, GPU-driver, package and event evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: USB boot, Linux GUI/all-package setup, apt intent, reboot, GUI display and event Criteria with source 5/30 timing are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind media and target identity to a pinned OS/desktop/graphics matrix, then demonstrate graphical login/session stability plus console fallback and event health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds reproducible package/driver control and GUI-specific evidence without automating the physical installer.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Post-boot collection may be assisted; physical/interactive installation and visual GUI acceptance remain manual.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Unpinned repositories can change kernel/desktop/driver combinations and invalidate reproducibility.

project_override_considerations: Project authority must define the exact GUI stack and whether broad apt upgrade is allowed; 'ubuntu-desktop' and 'all packages' do not uniquely specify a supported configuration.
expected_evidence: Critical approval, signed media and stable target/all-disk map
Graphical boot/login/session, resolution/display/KVM and console fallback evidence
Known-event triage, non-target preservation, recovery readiness and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently define physical USB Linux GUI installation and graphical/event acceptance.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Media, target, graphics/package matrix, operator and recovery are supplyable execution prerequisites; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Adds reproducible GUI/package/driver acceptance and rollback guards to the destructive operator-controlled USB installation.
independent_technical_reasoning: A system can boot successfully yet fail the GUI because the display manager, desktop session, kernel module or GPU/virtual-KVM path is incompatible. Therefore GUI acceptance needs a pinned graphics stack plus direct visual/session evidence and a console fallback; a generic package-install exit code is insufficient.
